UV_error_domain_and_payment: The existing dispersionUV_smooth_c2_dyadic_log_payment explicitly requires T<=x^(1/10). Original geometry only forces oldU below approximately X^(1/2), so this wrapper is unavailable in the general medium domain and nu<=1/10 must not be assumed.

The complete underlying SmoothErrorBounds U and V theorems are unconditional for arbitrary positive M and endpoints T,L>=1. Their errors are respectively C*(T*(1+log T)^(k-1))^2*(1+log L)^(8j), and C*(T*(1+log T)^(k-1))^2*L*(1+log L)^(5j-1).

The external coefficient second moment is bounded by sum_alpha_sq_dyadic_le at M=oldV and ell=2^B. Multiplying the U/V bounds therefore costs at most a fixed-order polylogarithm times oldV*(2oldU)^2*L.

Using the original, already-proved U*physicalFactorCap<=8X^(1-9sigma), oldV*(2oldU)^2*L=4X*(oldU*L)<=32X^(2-9sigma). Both U and V errors thus have a genuine fixed power saving after multiplication by the actual outer coefficient energy.

For fixed B,C0,sigma>0 and real target A, the fixed logarithm factors are absorbed by that 9sigma power slack with one threshold before every atom. This requires a new actual-geometry payment lemma, not a new analytic premise or a weakened modulus range.
